title: Florida public real-estate listing and distress-data source directory
scope: Prioritized discovery across Florida county, state, district and municipal sources, plus clearly labeled federal Florida coverage. Not an exhaustive audit of all 67 counties or every municipality.
verification: Official pages, indexed official material, vendor referral links and public metadata were reviewed. No production scraper, authenticated account, bulk download or full data-query workflow was tested. Direct local HTTP probes were prevented by environment DNS/network restrictions; that is not evidence a source blocks scraping.

priorities.P3: Empty feed, discovery-only entry or monitoring candidate

sources.collection_route: Public HTML listing; parse repeated labeled records.
sources.observation: Actual future sale records were readable. Fields: status, sale date, case number, judgment amount, parties, address and parcel ID. Page revised September 10, 2026. Auctions themselves are in person; online bidding is not necessary for online listing collection.

sources.observation: Collected 106 SW 10th Avenue, South Bay, scheduled September 23, 2026; $40,000 starting bid, $10,000 deposit, parcel ID and property facts. A starting bid is not a foreclosure judgment. Federal agency, not Florida state government.

sources.observation: Official entry and upcoming-auction shell read. No active Florida real-estate inventory verified. Separate from Treasury criminal-forfeiture real estate auctions.

sources.agency: U.S. Marshals Service / contracted real estate provider
sources.collection_route: Agency-designated contractor listings; confirm source attribution and browser access.
sources.observation: USMS page explicitly identifies RealLook as its real-property national contractor website. Contractor listings were not queried in this review.

sources.collection_route: Official association directory of county clerk websites and records contacts.
sources.observation: Use to expand county coverage and locate public exports or request existing electronic lists. Directory is not itself a property listing feed.

processing_notes: Keep judgment amount, opening bid, asking price and assessed value separate.
Deduplicate on source record/case and sale event, then link properties by county and parcel ID. A rescheduled auction is a status/history change.
Do not label a tax lien certificate sale as a real-property sale.
Do not label surplus proceeds, historical sales, litigation notices or government-owned inventories as current property listings.
Prefer published exports and documented APIs. Confirm terms and authorized automated access for each source; do not bypass account or anti-bot controls.

Polling suggestion: daily for listing changes, an additional status check near sale time, and weekly for low-volume surplus feeds. These are implementation recommendations, not published agency schedules.
